from_notes: EIA | Specific project before it starts; LCA | Product/process across its life – cradle to grave
x: EIA assesses the likely impacts of a specific project before it is implemented, while LCA follows a product or process from cradle to grave. Neither is limited to air pollution, design-stage location or one sector.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.67 (EIA = before implementation); LCA: app notes 5:77/5:78 (old-notes.txt) sub 1

x: EIA is the study of the likely environmental effects of a proposed project before it is approved; a census, pollution monitoring or plantation is not EIA.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC 12 (src/environment/nextgen-environment-appsc-12.txt) p.1 ('systematic evaluation of potential environmental impacts of proposed projects before implementation'); NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.67

x: A database is an organised collection of data that can be stored, manipulated and retrieved; it is not read-only, not limited to numbers and not merely a backup store. (ICT item, moved.)
source: general knowledge, not checked

x: MoEFCC launched the Green Skill Development Programme (pilot June 2017, full launch May 2018) under the ENVIS scheme to train youth for jobs in the environment, forest and wildlife sectors.
source: https://moef.gov.in/green-skill-development-program

from_notes: Noble M. Paikada (2024) | 2020 exemption for ordinary earth in linear projects – blanket exemption not upheld
x: Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India (SC, 21 March 2024) challenged item 6 of the 28 March 2020 notification, which exempted extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects such as roads and pipelines from environmental clearance; the Court struck the blanket exemption down as arbitrary (Article 14).
source: https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2024/03/26/supreme-court-strikes-blanket-exemption-under-ep-rules/; app notes 5:77/5:78 (old-notes.txt) sub 6

x: The NGT was set up on 18 October 2010 under the NGT Act 2010, which falls in the 11th Five Year Plan (2007-12). The 12th Plan began only in 2012.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.11 (established 18 October 2010); plan period: general knowledge, not checked

x: Silent Spring (1962), the book that launched the modern environmental movement against pesticides such as DDT, was written by Rachel Carson. Linda Buck, Gregg Semenza and Peter Ratcliffe are Nobel laureates in medicine. (Books-and-authors item, moved.)
source: general knowledge, not checked

x: On 3 July 2019 the Supreme Court told Meghalaya to deposit the Rs 100 crore the NGT had imposed (4 Jan 2019) for failing to curb illegal coal (rat-hole) mining; it allowed the money to be moved from the state's Environment Protection and Restoration Fund to the CPCB, for restoration only.
source: https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2019/07/03/sc-directs-meghalaya-govt-to-deposit-rs-100-crore-fine-for-illegal-coal-mining/

x: The National Bench of GSTAT is a forum of SECOND appeal (the first appeal lies to the appellate authority), and it is the first common forum of dispute resolution between the Centre and the States. So only b is correct. (GST item, moved.)
source: general knowledge, not checked (printed key)

x: The NGT Act provides for not less than 10 and up to 20 full-time judicial members (and as many expert members), not 5 to 10. source: general knowledge, not checked (printed key)

x: The National Green Tribunal (NGT Act 2010) was set up for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources. The National Environment Tribunal of 1995 never came into force.
source: Shankar Environment 10th ed. Part 21 (src/environment/shankar-environment-21.ocr.txt) p.19 (NGT Act preamble); NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.11

source: app notes 5:77/5:78 (old-notes.txt) 5:78 sub 8 ('BSI, ZSI | Kolkata'); BSI as a CITES scientific authority: PMF Environment Part 3 (src/environment/pmf-environment-03.txt) p.60

x: The World Conference on Environment in New Delhi (25-26 March 2017, inaugurated by President Pranab Mukherjee) was organised by the National Green Tribunal.
source: https://affairscloud.com/ngt-organises-world-conference-environment-new-delhi/

x: The NGT exists to decide cases on environmental protection and pollution control quickly. Monitoring pollution and setting emission or water-quality standards are regulator (CPCB/SPCB) jobs, not the tribunal's.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.11 ('Purpose → speedy disposal of environmental cases'); Shankar Environment 10th ed. Part 21 (src/environment/shankar-environment-21.ocr.txt) p.19

x: I is correct (NGT Act 2010). II is wrong: the NGT is not bound by the CPC 1908 and follows natural justice. III is wrong: the NGT sits at five places (Principal Bench New Delhi and zonal benches at Pune, Bhopal, Chennai and Kolkata), not six.
source: PMF Environment Part 6 (src/environment/pmf-environment-06.txt) p.94 (Principal Bench + 4 regional benches), p.95 (not bound by CPC)

x: The NGT's principal bench and headquarters are in New Delhi; Kolkata and Chennai host zonal benches, and Mumbai has none (the western bench is at Pune).
source: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.39 ('NGT … New Delhi'); PMF Environment Part 6 (src/environment/pmf-environment-06.txt) p.94

from_notes: Fly Ash Management and Utilization Mission constituted by NGT (January 2022)
x: In January 2022 the NGT constituted the Fly Ash Management and Utilization Mission to coordinate and monitor the handling, disposal and use of fly ash from coal thermal plants.
source: Shankar Environment Part 6 (src/environment/shankar-environment-06.ocr.txt) p.9 (mission 'directed by National Green Tribunal'); app notes 5:77/5:78 (old-notes.txt) 5:78 sub 4

from_notes: National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 | Strict liability for hazardous-substance accidents | Never brought into force; repealed by NGT Act 2010
x: The National Environment Tribunal Act was passed in 1995 (strict liability for hazardous-substance accidents) but never came into force; the NGT Act 2010 repealed it. 1997 is the NEAA Act.
source: app notes 5:77/5:78 (old-notes.txt) 5:78 sub 4 (predecessors table); NEAA 1997: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.12

x: India enacted the Biological Diversity Act in 2002 to conserve biodiversity, ensure its sustainable use and share benefits fairly, in line with the CBD.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.66 ('Biological Diversity Act 2002 – Biodiversity')

x: The Biological Diversity Act was passed in 2002 (amended 2023); the NBA under it was set up in 2003.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.66; Shankar Environment 10th ed. Part 21 (src/environment/shankar-environment-21.ocr.txt) p.16

x: A People's Biodiversity Register is a local-level record of biodiversity and the knowledge linked to it, prepared by the Biodiversity Management Committee with local people. It is not a list of protected areas or of endangered species.
source: Shankar Environment 10th ed. Part 21 (src/environment/shankar-environment-21.ocr.txt) p.17 (BMCs document local biodiversity and knowledge); PBR term: general knowledge, not checked

x: The National Biodiversity Authority was set up in 2003 to implement the Biological Diversity Act 2002, with its headquarters at Chennai (not Bengaluru or Hyderabad).
source: Shankar Environment 10th ed. Part 21 (src/environment/shankar-environment-21.ocr.txt) p.16 ('NBA – Chennai … established in 2003'); NextGen Rocket Environment (src/environment/rocket-environment.txt) p.40 ('Headquarters → Chennai')

from_notes: AP Environment Management Corporation (APEMCL): approved by AP cabinet (Nov 2019); collection, transport, storage and disposal of industrial waste in coordination with APPCB
